items.title: Mendeleev wrote out 63 cards and left blank spaces
items.claim: In 1869 Dmitri Mendeleev, writing a chemistry textbook in St Petersburg, sketched out the 63 known elements ordered by atomic mass. He noticed similar properties recur periodically. Where his pattern needed an element that didn't yet exist, he LEFT A GAP and predicted the properties of the missing element.
items.prompt: Why is Mendeleev's table considered a theory rather than a classification?

options.text: Because it was published in Russia
Because it predicted unknown elements (eka-aluminium, eka-boron, eka-silicon) whose properties were measured later and matched the predictions — gallium 1875, scandium 1879, germanium 1886
Because it was written by a famous chemist
Because it was rejected by other chemists

items.reveal_title: Predictions vindicated three times in 17 years
items.reveal:
Mendeleev's 1871 predictions for eka-silicon (germanium): atomic mass ~72, density ~5.5, grey metal, oxide formula MO2.

Winkler's 1886 germanium: atomic mass 72.6, density 5.32, grey metal, GeO2.

Mendeleev had also predicted eka-aluminium (gallium, found 1875 by Lecoq de Boisbaudran) and eka-boron (scandium, found 1879 by Nilson). All three matched closely.

He was passed over for the 1906 Nobel Prize in Chemistry — by ONE vote — in favour of Henri Moissan for isolating fluorine. He died in 1907. Element 101, mendelevium, was named in his honour in 1955.
items.why: A theory earns its keep by predicting what no one has measured. Mendeleev's table did this three times within his lifetime.

items.title: Wöhler made urea without a kidney in 1828
items.claim: Chemists in the 1820s believed organic compounds — substances found in living things — required a 'vital force' to be made. In 1828 Friedrich Wöhler, trying to make ammonium cyanate from inorganic precursors, accidentally produced urea — an organic substance found in mammalian urine.
items.prompt: Why did Wöhler's accident matter so much?

options.text: It made an organic compound from purely inorganic starting materials — the first crack in the doctrine that living things were chemically inaccessible to laboratory synthesis

items.reveal_title: The vital force begins to crack
items.reveal:
Wöhler had been heating ammonium chloride with silver cyanate. The product crystallised as colourless prisms. Analysis showed it was identical to urea — excreted by mammalian kidneys and definitively 'organic'.

He wrote to Berzelius: 'I must tell you that I can prepare urea without requiring a kidney of an animal, either man or dog.'

The vital force doctrine didn't die overnight. Urea is a borderline case — small, simple. But later syntheses (Kolbe's acetic acid in 1845, Berthelot's full organic synthesis programme in the 1850s-60s, Miller-Urey's amino acid synthesis in 1953) extended the principle until vitalism was indefensible.

Organic chemistry became 'the chemistry of carbon compounds', not 'the chemistry of life'.
items.why: A single accidental synthesis began the demolition of a centuries-old philosophical boundary between living and non-living chemistry.

items.title: A copper ion is colourless — and blue, and green
items.claim: Anhydrous CuSO4 is white. Add water and it turns vivid blue. Dissolve in concentrated HCl and it goes yellow-green. Same copper ion, drastically different colours.
items.prompt: What changes when ligands swap around the same Cu2+ centre?

options.text: Different ligands split the d-orbitals by different energies, so the wavelengths of light absorbed change, and the colour observed is the complementary colour of that wavelength
Water and chloride dissolve the copper, removing the colour

items.reveal_title: Crystal field theory — the geometry of d-orbitals
items.reveal:
Cu2+ has 9 d-electrons. In an octahedral field of ligands, the five d-orbitals split into two sets separated by an energy gap (delta-octahedral). A d-electron absorbs a photon and is promoted across this gap.

The gap depends on the ligand — the spectrochemical series ranks them: I- less than Br- less than Cl- less than H2O less than NH3 less than CN-. Larger gaps absorb shorter wavelengths. Cu(H2O)6 2+ absorbs orange (delta corresponding to ~600 nm), so it transmits blue. CuCl4 2- has a smaller gap, absorbs red, transmits yellow-green.

Anhydrous Cu2+ in CuSO4 has no significant ligand field at all — no splitting big enough for visible absorption — and so the salt is white.
items.why: Colour is treated as a fixed property of an element. It's actually a property of the coordination environment around a single ion.
